entityDescription:
Established in Milan in 1980, CSIL is an employee-owned research institute specialising in applied economics with specific expertise on research and innovation policy, industrial policy, regional development and market research. Since its origin, CSIL has been established as a centre of excellence concentrating on the diagnosis and design of sector strategies both for the public and private sectors, and the analysis of factors of competitiveness at regional, national and global levels.

In 40 years of activity, CSIL has gained considerable experience in supporting private and public decision making, working for EU and international clients including the European Commission, the European Parliament, the European Investment Bank, the African Development Bank, the OECD, the World Bank, CERN. For them, CSIL carried out comparative country analysis, reviews of policy frameworks and public expenditure planning and assessment to help understand the coherence and soundness of public interventions, as well as ex-ante, interim and ex-post evaluations to assess the economic and social effects which can be attributed to a policy, a programme, projects or individual measures.

CSIL has robust methodological expertise and developed guidelines and manuals related to the estimation of costs, benefits and impacts of policies, programmes and projects, as further explained in the next section with specific reference to research infrastructure and big science.

CSIL has strong credentials in various industry domains applications. For example, in the space industry CSIL has co-authored a study, on behalf of the European Commission DG GROW, aimed to investigate the feasibility and impacts of including societal criteria in the procurement activities of EU space programmes (‘A Study on Societal Criteria for Space Procurement’). In the same sector, CSIL researchers are collaborating with the University of Milan in the ‘Evaluation of the impact of the Italian Space Agency procurement activity on space industry’ (for the Italian Space Agency). The project aims to investigate and evaluate the economic benefits arising from public procurement on the full value chain, both upstream (R&D and realisation of key enabling space infrastructure and technologies) and downstream (products and services). In the past, CSIL contributed to the EU policy development process with the report ‘Space Market Uptake in Europe’, published by the European Parliament in 2015. This study analysed the potential impact on the downstream industry of the Galileo and Copernicus programmes and derived recommendations to improve the market uptake of space data.

In the field of EU research policy, in 2016-2017, CSIL delivered to the European Parliament three briefing papers on the ‘Implementation of Horizon 2020 – Societal Challenges from the Research and Industry Perspective’ focusing on the implementation of the programme’s three priorities – excellent science, industrial leadership, and societal challenges. In this field, CSIL provides consultancy to European institution as a member of various Framework Contracts, including those with the European Commission on ‘Ecosystem Support for Copernicus and the EU space policy’ and on ‘Studying, assessing and evaluating research and innovation programmes and policies’.

entityDescription:
Professionals take geodata driven decisions and improve decision-making with rapid geodata enrichment
Professionals across insurance, government, and public safety sectors (defense, health, emergency services) are responsible for evaluating environmental and infrastructure risks for properties, mission planning, or improving decision-making. Traditionally, these tasks require manually gathering, processing, and validating large volumes of geospatial data from diverse sources. This labor, cost and time-intensive process takes several hours or days to compete, demand specialized experience with data and/or geodata, which delays decision making and increase operational risks.
With Geoforge, these professionals can instantly enrich their existing data with geospatial data by submitting natural language queries such as "Show flood risks around these selected buildings or marker," or "Generate a terrain vulnerability analysis for this area of interest that I drew on the map."
Geoforge’s agentic AI (GeoLLM) retrieves, fuses, and processes relevant open local, regional, federal, global and proprietary datasets, including those stored via Geoforge's data warehouse (Motherduck or AWS S3) or accessed through partner APIs. Near real-time satellite imagery (optical, infrared, radar) is called using an API and and specialized GeoAI models (e.g., heatwave, flood, or landslide detection) are incorporated using 4EI's API (UK-based partner company of Ageospatial specialized in GeoAI natural disaster algorithms)
Within seconds, the platform produces interactive web reports or downloadable PDFs featuring maps, charts, elevation profiles, processed geodata in a standard format (.geoparquet / .geojson for vector and .cog for raster) ready to be downloaded and used. These instant outputs reduce analysis time by over 90% and cut operational costs by thousands of CHF per evaluation, but also empower users to make geodata-driven, timely decisions. It supports to reduce financial exposure and support geodata driven pricing, verify claims, avoid financial losses and support payout decisions (insurance), mission planning, ressource allocation and incrase sitautional awarness and support tactical decisions.

entityDescription:
Cosmic is an innovative start-up of very recent constitution (January 2020) but born from a well-tested team and expert in water loss, data transmission and cosmic rays. The idea, born in 2018, is to innovate the water loss research system with something that was a "disruptive technology" and not a simple improvement of existing techniques. To do this, Riccardo Marchetto, as it was for satellite leaks research with “Neptune S.r.l.”, (a company already incubated by ESA in 2014, thanks to BIC Lazio – Italy, for the water leaks detection with satellite images analysis), he was looking for a new space-derived technology to apply to daily water leaks issues with a TTP (Technology Transfer Project) from space technologies to terrestrial applications. The research gave its fruit with the possibility to control the ground humidity checking the absorption of cosmic rays. These radioactive rays coming from Space, with many sources like Sun's internal explosions or supernova explosions, are continuously bombarding the Earth and some of these rays are stopped only by hydrogen. Hydrogen is a component of water (H2O), where there is a loss there is a lot quantity of water mixed with the ground, and therefore a big quantity of hydrogen is present, so the neutron of cosmic rays is absorbed causing a decrease in its counting. The idea is cultivated by searching the market for the most difficult component to find: the neutron detector. It is from here that the meeting with Luca Stevanato, a PhD researcher at the University of Padua, who has realized such a device, comes out. A partnership aimed at conquering the market with this technology was immediately born. 
Cosmic is structurally much leaner waiting to receive the first orders but is still supported by Neptune's technical and commercial support. Within the structure, the team is composed by 8 employees who coordinate in order to manage the administrative, technical and on site work of the startup. Employees are young people under 40 and, together with Riccardo Marchetto (CEO), are working in the startup. They are Anna Tormen (24, Funds research and application), Schiesaro Carlo (40, specialist on water leak detection),and 3 teams active at all times for verifications and water leaks detection.

COBA provides engineering consultancy services ranging from basic and planning studies, technical, environmental and economic feasibility studies, preliminary design, design and construction design, design check, technical assistance, works supervision and project management, up to operation control and behaviour monitoring. Vast international experience in the fields of large hydraulic developments (namely dams, weirs, reservoirs, pumping systems and hydraulic structures), power generation (namely hydroelectric power projects) and transmission infrastructures, water supply and sanitation systems, water resources management plans, agriculture and rural development, transport infrastructures, geotechnical structures, environment, cartography and cadastre.
For this purpose, COBA relies on highly specialized multidisciplinary teams in its several areas of activity, from civil engineering – planning, geotechnics, structures, hydraulics, hydrology - to electromechanical and mechanical engineering, environmental engineering, agronomy and natural sciences, enabling the provision of state-of-the-art services and the preparation of studies / projects in an integrated manner. COBA’s mission is to comply with the Clients' requirements providing high standard engineering services, within the established delays and costs and to contribute to the reputation of the Portuguese Engineering worldwide.
With offices in three continents and experience in fifty-nine countries, COBA Group relies on the services of several companies, with specific fields of expertise or focal areas of activity. The close collaboration among all the Group’s companies allows the development of its activity in a complete way, by making use of its varied technical and logistical support all over the Group. 
In this way, COBA Group benefits from a deep interaction and a vast exchange of experience among the staff of several companies, which lead to synergies which enhance the specialized training of its members.
COBA has a permanent staff of about 200 people including the graduates, the technicians and the support staff. A significant number of their technicians have M.Sc. and PhD degrees obtained in Portuguese and/or Foreign Universities, with deep scientific and technical knowledge and a vast experience, forming the company’s nucleus of experts. The multidisciplinary teams cover all the sectors of activity of the company, thus allowing the permanent availability of all specialists necessary to the execution of studies and designs in an integrated and sustained basis, which is one of the basic principles of the firm.
COBA is a member of the Global Compact Network Portugal (GCNP), a Portuguese network of organisations representing the United Nations Global Compact (UN Global Compact), which is the United Nations’ corporate sustainability initiative.
GCNP is composed of national and international organizations operating in Portugal and aims to implement the Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact and the Sustainable Development Goals of United Nation’s 2030 Agenda by disseminating them to the interested parties and society at large, by sharing experiences among stakeholders worldwide.
COBA is NP ISO 45001:2019, NP EN ISO 14001:2015 and NP EN ISO 9001:2015 certified.

COMEX pioneered in the development of equipment for human intervention in extreme environments: The group led the way in industrial deep diving in the oil and gas supply and service sector. At the height of its activities, hundreds of divers from COMEX worked at depths of more than 300 meters, using helium-based breathing mixtures. COMEX¿ robots and equipment operate successfully at depths over 1000meter. 

The developments in the field of deep-sea intervention naturally led COMEX to participate in the development and test of equipment for human spaceflight: 
COMEX was involved in the verification of the European shuttle HERMES of the manned space flight program under the auspices of ESA. In the frame of these activities it participated in the test and development of equipment for EVA and IVA in its Neutral Buoyancy Facilities. Members of the European astronaut corps trained microgravity EVA in COMEX¿ test pools on real scale mock-ups of HERMES and COLUMBUS. 
COMEX is involved in the study of the SeaOrbiter, a new generation of exploration vessel, which is developed in cooperation with NASA¿s undersea training program. SeaOrbiter has multi-level pressure modules, used to prepare the technologies for long distance journeys in confined habitats.

The HYPERBARIC EXPERIMENTAL CENTRE is designed for studying the effects of pressure (hyperbaric and hypobaric) and gases (oxygen, nitrogen, helium and hydrogen etc.) on biological samples and structural models. The laboratory is equipped with a fully automated hypobaric/hyperbaric bio-incubator for tests with all gases, including hydrogen. Our team has successfully conducted more than 5300 operations, including nearly 2700 predominantly physiological or technological experimental human dives. 

This expertise gives COMEX today the necessary tools to develop, verify and test life support equipment and structural models for human intervention in hostile environments.

entityDescription: AI: Aerospace Innovation GmbH (AI) in Berlin develops special high-technology solutions and applications for the national and European aerospace industry and related agencies. AI is a precursor for new and innovative technologies, a provider of environmentally friendly and cost-efficient rocket propulsion systems for terrestrial and orbital operation as well as a centre of competence for strategic and technological space-related questions. Due to a long-standing experience in research and education along with extensive and detailed experimental work, AI is characterised by a unique technical know-how in the area of space transportation system design, rocket propulsion and propellant combustion as well as value analyses, cost modelling and modelling of complex socio-economic relations. AI was launched as an evolution of the aerospace engineering and consultancy company AI: Aerospace Institute, Lo, Adirim and Partners, that was founded in May 2000 within the frame of the Technology Transfer Program at Berlin University of Technology (TUB). When AI was founded in 2007 in order to provide complete system solutions and products in the field of aerospace propulsion, the core activities of AI: Aerospace Institute were transferred to the new company. Today, the team of AI consists of eight employees and two consultants. The company presently focuses on space transportation and propulsion system investigations as well as trend analyses, while the range of activities includes numerical simulations of complex dynamic processes, e.g. solid and hybrid rocket motor combustion, feasibility investigations for new technologies and systems as well as development and manufacturing of demonstrators and prototypes for customised propulsion solutions.

Keyrus Belgium is part of the Keyrus Group, a global consulting and technology company specializing in data intelligence, digital experience, and business transformation. Beyond technology, Keyrus Belgium supports clients in rethinking and optimizing their operating models, processes, and organizational structures.
